channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Constructs Pipeline to China for $327 Million, Potentially Filling it with Russian Oil
item.description: Kazakhstan is building a pipeline to China valued at $327 million. Reports suggest that Russian oil may be used to fill this new infrastructure, raising questions about the energy flow and partnerships involved in the project.

item.title: Former Employee of "Government for Citizens" Corporation Sentenced for Illegal Gold Mining
item.description: In Oskemen, a former deputy director of the "Government for Citizens" state corporation and another individual were sentenced to four years in prison for organizing illegal gold mining. They used a subsidiary company with only an exploration license to extract over 15 kg of gold, causing significant environmental damage.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Finance Explains When Tax Authorities Monitor Expenses
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Finance, Asset Tursunov, clarified that tax authorities will question individuals whose expenses, such as purchasing property or vehicles, significantly exceed their declared income without other verifiable sources. Taxpayers can resolve such issues by declaring additional income and paying relevant taxes.

item.title: New 'Bishkek Arena' Opens in Kyrgyzstan with Concert Featuring Dozens of Stars
item.description: Kyrgyzstan officially opened its new 'Bishkek Arena', attracting tens of thousands of spectators. The event featured over 60 artists from various countries, including a significant delegation from Kazakhstan. Highlights included a duet by Kairat Nurtas and Mirbek Atabekov, a performance by young drummer Amir Maximilian from Almaty, and appearances by Redfoo and Party Rock Crew. President Sadyr Japarov also made an appearance.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Commercial Self-Driving Taxi Services by 2028
item.description: Kazakhstan is preparing to launch commercial self-driving taxi services and drone delivery by 2028. Legislative changes are in place to support the operation of autonomous vehicles and the development of necessary infrastructure. Pilot programs for self-driving taxis are underway in Astana, Almaty, and Kosshy, with drone delivery trials active in Almaty.

item.title: Car Dealership Director Sentenced for Defrauding Clients of 128 Million Tenge
item.description: A car dealership director in Astana has been sentenced to six years and eight months in prison for defrauding six clients of over 128 million tenge. The director promised to import cars from China but used the funds for personal purposes, providing falsified documents to deceive buyers.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Pilot New Smart System for Traffic Management in Major Cities
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to implement a new smart system to manage traffic flow in its major cities. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has tasked the Ministry of Transport and local administrations with identifying high-load roads for a two-month pilot project. The system aims to monitor real-time conditions and predict congestion, with successful solutions to be expanded.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Digitalization Efforts Save Government 200 Billion Tenge Annually
item.description: Digitalization in Kazakhstan is projected to save up to 200 billion tenge in annual budget funds. According to the Finance Minister, the state can now track every tenge from the budget and assess its efficiency. By planning the 2027-2029 budget, expenditures totaling 1.5 trillion tenge have already been prevented.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Launch Commercial Air Taxi Services by 2028
item.description: Commercial air taxi services are planned to launch in Kazakhstan by 2028, according to Deputy Prime Minister Zhanaslan Madiev. A three-year pilot project for unmanned taxis is currently underway in Astana, Almaty, and Kosshy. Drone delivery has also been initiated in Almaty, with legislative changes supporting air taxi operations.

item.title: Almaty to use AI-powered cameras for identifying people, cars, and protests
item.description: Almaty's digitalization department plans to spend 129.7 million tenge to upgrade the Target EYE public safety platform. The system will integrate an AI module to analyze city camera footage, searching for individuals, vehicles, and events via text queries. This aims to help operators quickly find important occurrences and objects.

item.title: Kazakhstan to introduce temporary restrictions on social media accounts for under-16s
item.description: Kazakhstan is preparing amendments to change the registration process for individuals under 16 on online platforms. If passed, platforms will need to verify users' ages, with separate regulations detailing how this will be done. Potential methods include facial recognition and analyzing account activity.

item.title: Kazakhstan's vice-minister clarifies AI's role and responsibility in social benefit payments
item.description: Kazakhstan's First Vice-Minister of Digital Development, Rostislav Konyashkin, stated that human employees, not AI, are responsible for errors in social benefit payments. AI analyzes data and provides recommendations, but the final decision and transaction rest with the authorized employee.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Use AI for Age Verification on Social Media Platforms
item.description: The Kazakh government is preparing amendments to regulate the registration of users under 16 on online platforms. Proposed measures may involve artificial intelligence to verify age through facial images, content, subscriptions, and account activity, while protecting personal data. A transition period will be provided, and accounts of underage users may be temporarily suspended.

item.title: UAE Extradites Three Suspects Wanted by Kazakhstan for Criminal Charges
item.description: The United Arab Emirates has extradited three individuals to Kazakhstan who were internationally wanted for criminal prosecution. One suspect defrauded a victim of $368,000 in Astana. Another is accused of aggravated assault and robbery in Almaty, and the third allegedly stole $24,200 in Astana. All are now in pre-trial detention.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Develop Domestic Robot Production with International Partners
item.description: Kazakhstan is initiating projects to develop its own robot production, focusing on technology localization, research, and skills transfer. The Ministry of Digital Development announced that projects in Astana and Almaty are underway with international partners. The goal is to train engineers and establish domestic manufacturing capabilities, with factory construction planned for next year.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reduces New Public Service Center Hires, Requiring Retraining for Existing Staff
item.description: Kazakhstan is reducing the recruitment of new employees for Public Service Centers (TsONs) as many existing workers must retrain. This is due to the near-completion of online services. The Ministry of Digital Development stated that the number of citizen inquiries has already decreased by 30% thanks to digitalization efforts.

item.title: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Meets with UNESCO Representative to Discuss Water and Cryosphere Initiatives
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin met with UNESCO's acting Assistant Director-General for Natural Sciences, Abu Amani. They discussed the implementation of the Decade of Action for the Cryosphere (2025–2034) and preparations for the 2028 UN Water Conference in Dushanbe. Cooperation in water resources, glacier studies, and science was also reviewed.

item.title: Israel prepared to shoot down Flydubai flight, citing 9/11-like attack prevention protocols
item.description: Israeli media reports indicate Israel was prepared to shoot down a Flydubai flight, citing a special protocol to prevent attacks similar to 9/11. The Prime Minister holds the sole authority to order such an action.

item.title: Kazakhstan Participates in Moscow Consultations on Afghanistan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Special Representative for Afghanistan, Yerkin Tukumov, attended the 8th Moscow Format consultations. Discussions covered Afghanistan's political and economic situation, regional security, counter-terrorism, and cooperation with Kabul. Kazakhstan noted increased trade and interest in expanding economic ties and infrastructure projects.

item.title: Kazakh Citizens in Russia Appeal for Help Amidst Mobilization Concerns
item.description: Kazakh citizens who went to Russia for work are appealing for help, stating they have only three days left before potential deployment to conflict zones. They claim they were forced to sign documents for combat and are seeking assistance from Kazakh authorities to return home safely. The Foreign Ministry is reportedly aware of the situation.

item.title: Thirty US States Urge Supreme Court to Release Afghan Assets for 9/11 Victims
item.description: Attorneys general from 30 US states have asked the Supreme Court to review a case concerning approximately $3.5 billion in frozen Da Afghanistan Bank assets. Victims and families of the September 11 attacks seek these funds for compensation, having secured nearly $17 billion in judgments. A previous ruling denied access to these specific assets.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Launch Six New Earth Remote Sensing Satellites
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to develop six new Earth remote sensing satellites, according to Minister of Digital Development, Innovations and Aerospace Industry Zhaslan Madiev. Currently, three satellites are operational in the Earth remote sensing system. The country also plans to create KazSat-3R by 2029 to replace existing communication satellites.

item.title: Digitalization Efforts Save State Budget Up To 200 Billion Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's digitalization initiatives have helped reduce state expenditures and increase budget revenues, according to Finance Minister Madi Takiev. The implementation of a special tax regime for self-employed individuals on digital platforms has significantly increased social payments. A unified digital system for budget planning and procurement enhances financial oversight and efficiency.

item.title: Central Asian Rights Groups Report Increased Repression Ahead of OSCE Conference
item.description: Human rights advocates have issued a joint statement ahead of the OSCE conference in Warsaw, detailing a rise in repression against independent organizations, journalists, and activists across Central Asia. The statement highlights concerns over laws affecting foreign representatives in Kyrgyzstan and reporting requirements for foreign funding recipients in Kazakhstan, alongside NGO closures in Tajikistan.

item.title: Yemeni Forces Capture Strategic Strait, Houthis Retreat Inland
item.description: Yemeni government forces, backed by Saudi airstrikes, have retaken the coast around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and advanced to the outskirts of Mocha. Houthi fighters are reportedly retreating. The Defense Ministry stated the city has fallen. The Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi targets, which could not be immediately verified.

item.title: CENTCOM Reports 130 Ships Rerouted Due to U.S. Naval Blockade of Iran
item.description: The U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that 130 commercial vessels have been rerouted as of October 5 due to a high-intensity naval blockade of Iran. Commander Brad Cooper stated that swift action would be taken against any vessel attempting to evade the blockade. This comes amid claims that Iran has been unable to export crude oil recently.

item.title: Pakistani company plans to establish olive plantation on 500 hectares in Jizzakh region
item.description: Pakistan's WaterCon company intends to implement an investment project to create an olive plantation spanning 500 hectares in the Yangiobod district of Jizzakh region, Uzbekistan. A memorandum of understanding has been signed between the company and the Jizzakh regional administration. The project aims to cultivate and process olives, establishing a full production cycle.

item.title: US Central Command Claims Destruction of 13 Commercial Ships in Three Months
item.description: US Central Command (CENTCOM) reported destroying 13 commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz over the past three months. CENTCOM stated these vessels were attempting to enter or exit Iranian ports, or were part of a multi-billion dollar network linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

item.title: New Hydropower Plant 'Khutalon' Planned Between Rogun and Nurek Dams in Tajikistan
item.description: A new hydropower plant, 'Khutalon,' with a capacity of 800 MW, is planned to be constructed between the Rogun and Nurek dams in Tajikistan. This project aims to further develop the country's hydroelectric power generation capabilities.

item.title: Former Kyrgyzstan Transport Minister Nurlan Sulaymanov Arrested in Bishkek
item.description: Nurlan Sulaymanov, former Minister of Transport and Communications of Kyrgyzstan, was detained by the Interior Ministry on October 3rd and subsequently arrested by a Bishkek court on October 5th. The specific charges against him remain officially undisclosed. Sulaymanov served as minister from 2005-2010 under President Kurmanbek Bakiyev and was later a Member of Parliament.

item.title: Competition Committee Reports Companies with Most Online Trade Complaints
item.description: In early 2026, 19.2% of consumer protection complaints, totaling 1230, were related to e-commerce. The Competition Committee identified systemic issues including transparency, electronic contracts, and dispute resolution.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches 13 Criminal Cases After Ministry of Defense Inspection
item.description: Following a comprehensive inspection of the Ministry of Defense, Kazakhstan has initiated 13 criminal cases. These cases involve alleged embezzlement of state property, abuse of office, and other violations. The inspection was prompted by the deaths of servicemen during exercises and revealed systemic issues within the armed forces.

item.title: Uzbekistan MFA: Latvia Not Limiting Visa Issuance to Uzbek Citizens
item.description: Latvia has informed Tashkent that it sees no need to change the current visa issuance procedures for Uzbek citizens, according to the Uzbek Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Negotiations were held between the Uzbek embassy in Riga and Latvian officials. The Uzbek MFA conveyed its position on the potential impact of proposed measures on bilateral relations.

item.title: Tajikistan participates in C5+1 SI conference on AI in Astana
item.description: A Tajik delegation attended the C5+1 SI conference in Astana, Kazakhstan, focusing on artificial intelligence development, digital cooperation, and technological partnerships between Central Asia and the US. Tajikistan presented its AI and digital transformation achievements.

item.title: UNAMA Head Rabab Fatima Seeks Continued UN General Assembly Support
item.description: Rabab Fatima, UN Special Representative for Afghanistan and head of UNAMA, has requested ongoing support from the UN General Assembly President for the mission. Fatima met with the President and expressed gratitude for his commitment to vulnerable countries. She emphasized the importance of his continued backing for UNAMA's mandate, particularly in his new role.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Blogger Sirojiddin Adilov Sentenced to Four Years for Extortion and Fraud
item.description: In Uzbekistan, blogger Sirojiddin Adilov has been sentenced to four years in prison by the Mirzacho'l District Court for extortion and fraud. While the court stated charges were not related to his social media activity, human rights advocates link his prosecution to his critical online posts. The blogger plans to appeal.

item.title: US Special Envoy: Trump expressed desire to visit Uzbekistan
item.description: US Special Presidential Envoy for Global Partnership, Paolo Zampolli, stated that President Trump wishes to visit Uzbekistan. While no date is set, Zampolli confirmed Trump's intention to visit, citing a strong personal connection with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

item.title: Iran Offers Cooperation on Afghan Infrastructure Projects
item.description: Iran has offered to cooperate with Afghanistan on major infrastructure and development projects, including the Herat-Mazar-e-Sharif railway, mining, and power generation. The offer was made during a meeting between Afghan Deputy Foreign Minister Mohammad Naeem and Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister for Economic Diplomacy Hamid Qanbari.

item.title: Six Uzbek Citizens Extradited from UAE After International Search
item.description: Six Uzbek citizens, wanted internationally via Interpol for various crimes, have been extradited from the United Arab Emirates to Uzbekistan. This operation is the result of years of cooperation between the Interpol bureaus and authorities of both countries. Since the beginning of the year, 16 individuals have been extradited from the UAE.

item.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey Agree to Deploy Forces Under Mecca Defense Pact Amid Regional Tensions
item.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey have agreed to rapidly deploy forces and military capabilities in Saudi Arabia under the Mecca Defense Pact. The decision followed an emergency meeting of the "Political and Defense Strategic Committee" in Riyadh. The move aims to implement collective defense commitments amid security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, though no specific threat was identified.
